note: Track double-stops (guitar-caged), step 2: 3rds on the G and B strings, frets 0 to 7, on the double-stops-neck at level beginner (tapped and copied, then up and back with each chord named), then the root and 3rd of each chord of a G, C, G, D backing track in a tab play-along, the pair and its two notes in turn (folded in from guitar-beginner-thirds-on-strings-3-2). The text carries no frets; the key moves, so the play-along's shape names its key and its grips move with it.

exercise.title: {{=key}} major in 3rds on the G and B strings
exercise.why: A 3rd on the G and B strings has only two shapes, both notes in one fret or the B string one fret lower, so a whole key is those two shapes moved along the two strings.

cells.text:
Tap the lowest double stop on the neck below to hear it, then play it: the G and B strings struck together. Go up the neck one double stop at a time, tapping it and then playing it.
Practice until your hand finds each one after a single look.

Press Play below to hear the 3rds up the neck and back down. Then play them yourself the same way, one double stop per slow beat, and say the name of the chord above each one as you play it.
Each double stop is the lowest two notes of that chord, and the ringed note, on the G string, is its root.

Press Play below to start the backing track: four chords, a bar each. On each chord, play its root and 3rd together, then the lower note alone, both again, then the higher note alone.
When the chord changes, the shape stays the same and only the fret is new.
{{?key}}In another key the frets are new, and the 3rd of a major chord still has both notes in one fret.
